I am 69, I never went to school, not even one day. I learned everything from my mother-in-law and from watching the neighbors. I have farmed these 7 mu for 47 years. It is just me and my old man now, two mouths to eat from this land.

For wheat, I do what I did last year. I rotary till the ground before sowing in October. I buy improved wheat seed from the dealer — the same kind my neighbor Lao Zhang used last year because his crop looked good. I sow 30 jin per mu, which is about 15 kg. Before sowing I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, 50 kg. Then at green-up time in March I spread another 50 kg bag of compound, and at jointing I add half a bag of urea, 25 kg. I would rather put a little too much than too little — if the wheat goes yellow, I lose everything. I irrigate three times: winter water before the freeze, jointing water, and filling water when the grain is swelling. That well water is my life. I spray three times: herbicide once in early spring, insecticide once when the aphids come, and fungicide once because two years ago my neighbor got rust and I do not want that. I expect 900 jin per mu, about 450 kg.

For maize, I plant right after cutting wheat in June — no time to plow, I plant no-tillage. I use hybrid seed, bought from the dealer in packages, about 1 package per mu. At planting I put down one and a half bags of compound fertilizer, about 75 kg per mu. I do not usually topdress maize because by August I am tired and the corn is already tall, but I water it twice if the rain does not come — once when it is knee-high and once when the ears are filling. I spray three times: herbicide once right after planting, and insecticide twice because those armyworms always show up in July. If Lao Zhang sprays three times, I spray three times. I expect 1000 jin per mu, about 500 kg.

Money is tight. Compound fertilizer is 130 yuan a bag and urea is 90 yuan. But I have seen what happens when you skimp — the yield drops and then you cry. So I buy what I bought last year, and I watch my neighbors.
